documents: Cenki, Rey, Arcay & Giordani 2022, Terra Nova 34:193-200, published paper (PDF)

entry.evidence: the detailed processes involved in their formation remain unresolved and notably the sequence of appearance and duration of migmatisation

sequences.source_document: Cenki et al. 2022, Terra Nova 34:193-200 (published PDF)

steps.action: The authors pose the question of the timing, duration and volume of migmatite and granulite formation in the orogenic cycle, which the rock record does not resolve.
steps.quote: the respective timing, duration and volume of migmatites and granulites are difficult to extract from the rocks archive

steps.action: They take Harley's (2016) proposal from the literature: slow, long-lived granulites form in large hot orogens and fast episodes in back-arc settings.
steps.quote: episodes of granulite-facies metamorphism may be restricted to back-arc settings

steps.action: They solve the steady-state heat equation to map Moho temperature against crustal and lithospheric thickness for moderate and high, uniform and differentiated radiogenic heat production (RHP) and a range of basal heat flows.
steps.quote: the solution of the steady-state heat equation allows for the prediction of the equilibrium geotherm

steps.action: They compare the equilibrium Moho temperatures with the granulite and migmatite stability fields. At moderate RHP a crust thicker than 70 km is needed; at high RHP a 40-km crust reaches these conditions.
steps.quote: continental crusts must achieve a thickness >70 km to experience granulite facies conditions

steps.action: Citing Bailey (1999), they drop the thermal-equilibrium assumption, because such a hot crust would collapse gravitationally.
steps.quote: such high temperatures are unsustainable on long time scales as such a hot crust would collapse

steps.action: They retain the sub-claim that total RHP and its distribution in the crust control the conditions for HT-UHT rocks, consistent with cited studies.
steps.quote: This confirms that the conditions to form significant volumes of HT-UHT rocks can be controlled by the total RHP

steps.action: They refine the question to the additional effect of tectonic velocity on the tempo and duration of migmatite and granulite conditions over a full orogenic cycle.
steps.quote: 2D thermo-mechanical experiments of a complete orogenic cycle allow to explore the additional effect of the tectonic velocities

steps.action: They use the Underworld open-source finite element code, developed partly by co-authors (Beucher et al. 2019; Mansour et al. 2020).
steps.quote: The numerical models are performed with Underworld, a well-tested open-source finite element code

steps.action: They design a 480 x 160 km 2D model on a 240 x 80 grid with three stages: shortening at slow (0.24 cm/yr) or fast (2.4 cm/yr) velocity, a basal heat flow rise mimicking delamination, then extensional relaxation.
steps.quote: Each model runs through three stages

steps.action: They set two end-member crusts from literature RHP estimates: uniform RHP of about 1 for the Phanerozoic, and differentiated RHP of about 2 for the Proterozoic, with crustal thickness chosen to give a 650°C initial Moho.
steps.quote: Models RHP2_diff aim at approaching thermal conditions of a differentiated crust prevailing during the Proterozoic.

steps.action: They run the four experiments and track the onset and extent of partial melting and granulite conditions through time (Figures 2 and 3).
steps.quote: In models RHP2_diff, the production of migmatites occurs at the onset of crustal thickening

steps.action: They compare the models' outcomes and PTt paths (Figure 4) across RHP structure and shortening velocity. RHP2_diff crust crosses into the sillimanite field; RHP1_unif crust stays in kyanite.
steps.quote: This strongly contrasts with models RHP1_unif, in which the continental crust remains in the kyanite stability field (Figure 4c,d).

steps.action: They compare the model prograde granulites passing through the sillimanite field with published natural HT-UHT terranes (Figure 4e).
steps.quote: prograde granulites evolving through the sillimanite field, similar to many HT-UHT terranes

steps.action: They propose localized deep-crustal granulites in a less radiogenic crust under slow shortening as a further route besides Harley's back-arc setting.
steps.quote: This case highlights another way to form localized granulites

steps.action: They compare Slw_RHP1_unif with the Variscan crust (late-orogenic granulite xenoliths, granulite lenses) and with the Bohemian Massif parametric model of Maierovà et al. (2014).
steps.quote: This model may be an analogue for the Variscan crust

steps.action: They keep Slw_RHP2_diff (differentiated, radiogenic crust with slow shortening) as the best explanation of long-lived regional HT-UHT terranes.
steps.quote: is best explained by the model Slw_RHP2_diff

steps.action: They compare model PTt path shapes with natural and modelled paths: the Grenville model, In Ouzzal, Mather gneisses, Palni Hills (isothermal decompression), and southern India (isobaric heating and cooling).
steps.quote: Other granulitic terranes present near-isothermal decompression paths culminating at 8–13 kbar

steps.action: They conclude that the interplay of total RHP, its distribution and shortening velocity explains PTt paths and the relative tempo of migmatite and granulite formation.
steps.quote: the interplay between total RHP, its distribution and shortening velocities can explain PTt paths for dominantly granulitic or migmatitic terranes

tree.answer: Yes: long-lived HT-UHT granulitic terranes in the rock record
No: timing and sequence of melting and granulite formation are not accessible from rocks
Tempo and duration of migmatite and granulite conditions in the orogenic cycle
Parameter end-members (RHP amount and distribution, slow or fast shortening); Harley's large-hot-orogen versus back-arc settings
Yes: models predict different onset times, volumes and PTt path shapes
Not tested: no sensitivity, resolution or repeat runs reported
Slow shortening of a radiogenic, differentiated crust best explains long-lived HT-UHT terranes

end.claim: A differentiated, highly radiogenic crust under slow shortening forms large volumes of prograde migmatites throughout the orogenic cycle and granulites mainly during collapse, best explaining long-lived regional HT-UHT terranes and their PTt paths.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the 2D thermo-mechanical runs of full orogenic cycles, which yield the timing of melting and granulite onset and the PTt paths, there is no tempo or path prediction to compare with the rock record.

gates.evidence: No data were acquired. The end-member models were chosen from literature RHP values to explore parameters, not to test a stated hypothesis. The comparison with natural PT paths (Figure 4e) could in principle have failed, but it is qualitative and has no metric. Nothing is reported as fixed in advance.

imports.item: Lagrangian integration point finite element method (Moresi et al. 2003, Journal of Computational Physics) implemented in Underworld
National Computational Infrastructure and Pawsey Supercomputing Centre resources

novelty_claims.quote: This paper is innovative in the sense that it illustrates this problem in a dynamic manner.
We address the intertwined timing of partial melting and granulite formation during the genesis of HT-UHT terranes in a manner that cannot be derived from [...]
This case highlights another way to form localized granulites in addition to the back-arc geodynamic settings suggested by Harley (2016).

limits: Process gaps. No sensitivity or resolution tests are reported: no grid refinement of the 240 x 80 mesh, no rheology or parameter variation beyond the four designed runs, and no repeat runs. The Significance statement claims reproducibility via open-source code, but no reproduction is performed. The Supporting Information (setup, parameters, script) was not supplied to the coder. Comparison with natural PT paths is visual and qualitative (Figure 4e), with no misfit measure. Inference: the RHP1_unif and RHP2_diff models differ at once in total RHP, RHP distribution and initial crustal thickness (40 vs 35 km), so their effects are confounded. Peer review is acknowledged but no review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. Composition none_fits: this is a parametric forward-modelling study whose conditions are set numerically and compared afterwards with cited natural analogues; it is not strong inference, not a trace series (conditions set, not found), and not forecast verification. Sub-claims and their statuses: (a) total RHP and its distribution control equilibrium HT-UHT potential, a derived expectation consistent with cited work (regularity_in_range, inference); (b) localized granulites can form in a less radiogenic crust under slow shortening as an alternative to back-arc settings (best_explanation, hypothesis level); (c) Slw_RHP1_unif as an analogue for the Variscan crust (best_explanation, suggestive). V is none: the only checks are agreements with other groups' models (Maierovà et al. 2014; Jamieson et al. 2010), coded as not performed here.

disagreements.target: Harley (2016): fast or localized granulite-facies metamorphism restricted to back-arc settings
disagreements.support: Model Slw_RHP1_unif forms a localized granulite-cored migmatitic dome in the deep crust during slow shortening and collapse, without a back-arc setting.
disagreements.quote: This case highlights another way to form localized granulites in addition to the back-arc geodynamic settings suggested by Harley (2016).

alternatives_considered.chosen: 2D non-steady-state thermo-mechanical experiments of a full orogenic cycle
alternatives_considered.reason: equilibrium conditions unsustainable because a hot crust would collapse (Bailey 1999)

alternatives_considered.chosen: both end-members modelled: uniform RHP about 1 (Phanerozoic) and exponentially differentiated RHP about 2 (Proterozoic)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: uniform versus differentiated RHP distribution; moderate versus high total RHP
alternatives_considered.reason: literature estimates of present-day crust (Taylor & McLennan 1995) and of higher, upper-crust-enriched Proterozoic RHP (Mareschal & Jaupart 2013; Artemieva et al. 2017; Gard et al. 2019; Alessio et al. 2020; Goes et al. 2020)

alternatives_considered.alternatives: slow (0.24 cm/yr over 70 My) versus fast (2.4 cm/yr over about 7 My) shortening
alternatives_considered.reason: to explore the effect of tectonic velocity on tempo

alternatives_considered.chosen: 35-km initial crust for RHP2_diff, 40-km for RHP1_unif
alternatives_considered.reason: none given explicitly; each choice yields an initial Moho temperature of about 650°C
